analysis.investment_thesis: Cohance Lifesciences (formerly Suven Pharma) presents a deeply troubling combination — operating margins have collapsed from ~44% in FY2022 to just 8.89% today, net profit has fallen 42% from peak, and yet the stock trades at an extraordinary 94.69x EV/EBITDA. A concurrent corporate restructuring (balance sheet nearly tripling in one year to INR 5,568 Cr) and a sudden borrowings spike from INR 65 Cr to INR 451 Cr add opacity precisely when clarity is most needed.
key_strengths: CDMO sector has durable secular tailwinds — global pharma companies are actively diversifying manufacturing away from China, benefiting Indian CDMOs
Forward P/E of 35.86 versus trailing 49.70 implies the market believes a meaningful earnings recovery is underway — if that materializes, downside is partially bounded
Revenue has grown at a 21.2% CAGR over 6 years, demonstrating real top-line capability even as margins have compressed
key_risks: Catastrophic margin deterioration: EBITDA margins fell from ~44% (FY2022) to ~35% (FY2025 implied) and operating margins to just 8.89% — this looks structural, not cyclical, following the corporate restructuring
Net profit has declined from INR 454 Cr (FY2022) to INR 265 Cr (FY2025) — a 42% fall from peak — while the market cap has not corrected proportionally, creating extreme valuation risk

Balance sheet opacity: total assets jumped from INR 2,254 Cr (FY2024) to INR 5,568 Cr (FY2025) and borrowings from INR 65 Cr to INR 451 Cr — the nature and economics of this transformation remain unclear
red_flags: EV/EBITDA of 94.69x — among the most extreme valuations possible for an industrial manufacturer; this prices in not just recovery but a return to record profits AND substantial multiple expansion
Operating income has been contracting over the last 5 years (573 Cr in FY2022 → 374 Cr in FY2025) even as revenue nominally expanded — a classic sign of deteriorating unit economics
Abrupt 7x increase in borrowings in a single year (INR 65 Cr → INR 451 Cr) during a period of declining profits raises questions about the financial urgency behind the restructuring
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Cohance is a company in fundamental transition — the name change from Suven Pharmaceuticals, the balance sheet nearly tripling in one year, and the simultaneous borrowings spike from INR 65 Cr to INR 451 Cr all point to a major acquisition or demerger that has yet to demonstrate value creation. What was once a high-margin CDMO (44% EBITDA margins in FY2022) is now reporting 8.89% operating margins — a transformation that is decidedly not in shareholders' favor. EBITDA has fallen from INR 639 Cr (FY2022) to INR 419 Cr (FY2025) despite the enlarged asset base.

At 94.69x EV/EBITDA, the market is pricing in a recovery that would require margins to return toward historical peaks — but there is zero evidence in the financial trajectory that this is occurring. The forward P/E of 35.86 still implies a business trading at a massive premium to even its optimistic earnings scenario. The combination of declining fundamentals, corporate opacity, and extreme valuation is precisely the situation Marks warns about: consensus optimism in the face of deteriorating facts. The probability of permanent capital loss here is material.
